title: A sign of unity (Lumen Gentium 1)
hook: the Church is a kind of sacrament of unity for all people
tomorrow: a seven-year-old asks where God lives. who answers first?

segments.voice: This week opened the Church's documents: numbered paragraphs, God speaking as to friends, word and body, summit and font, and full and active. Yesterday's line was full and active.
screen: `FULL AND ACTIVE.` → `THE WEEK, IN FIVE DOCUMENTS.`

segments.voice: A field full of folding chairs at a graduation: families who pray five different ways, some who don't pray at all, all clapping for the same kids. The council's document on the Church opens on a crowd bigger than that. Its first words, Lumen Gentium, mean the light of the nations, and the light it names is Christ, not the Church. The Church comes a breath later, as the place that light shines from. So who is that light for?
screen: `FOLDING CHAIRS, ONE FIELD.` → `THE LIGHT OF THE NATIONS.` → `WHO IS IT FOR?`

segments.voice: Read the first paragraph in steps. First, the light. Christ is the light of the nations, and the council longs to bring that light, shining on the face of the Church, to everyone, by preaching the gospel to every creature. That's Mark's Gospel: "Go ye into the whole world, and preach the gospel to every creature." Second, the sentence that names the day. The Church, it says, is in Christ like a sacrament, a sign and an instrument. Notice the hedge: like a sacrament. Something that works the way a sacrament works, showing a reality and helping bring it about. Third, a sign of what? Two unions at once: a close union with God, and the unity of the whole human race. Not the unity of one club. The whole human race. Fourth, why the council said it then. People, it says, are being drawn closer by social, technical and cultural ties, and it hopes they'll also reach full unity in Christ. That's a Catholic hope, said in Catholic words. One to tell a friend: the document on the Church doesn't open with the Church at all. It opens with a light meant for everyone.
screen: `CHRIST, THE LIGHT OF THE NATIONS.` · `LIKE A SACRAMENT: SIGN AND INSTRUMENT.` · `UNION WITH GOD, AND ALL PEOPLE.` · `DRAWN CLOSER, HOPING FOR MORE.` · then, large: `A SIGN FOR ALL.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one person on the other side of some line from you: another faith, no faith, an old argument. Send them one short, warm line that asks for nothing back. If you pray, you can hold them in the same light as yourself while it sends.
A sign of unity. Lumen Gentium's picture of the Church: like a sacrament, showing and serving union with God and among all people. Today's word.
Your line: a sign for all. A lamp held up, not a wall built around. That's the week.

howItsDone: Catholics often quote Lumen Gentium 1 when speaking of the Church's mission to the world and of prayer for unity, including gatherings with Christians of other churches and with people of other faiths.

fork.setup: at a city service for people of many faiths, a speaker says 'one human family, praying different ways.' your cousin calls it watering down the faith. what does Lumen Gentium 1 add?
options: the Church calls itself a sign of the whole human race's unity, while naming Christ as the light.
the Church speaks about unity only among its own members.
the council says every religion is the same, so the differences don't matter.
fork.reveal: Lumen Gentium 1 names Christ as the light and calls the Church a sign of union with God and of the unity of the whole human race: one family, honest differences.

original.note: Latin in Lumen Gentium 1: the Church is like a sacrament, a sign and instrument.

what a scholar hears: 'veluti sacramentum', a hedged term, and a Church whose face reflects a light that is not its own.

chat.says: gave the speech!! ended on 'one human family.' mia's mom cried. ok but is that a catholic thing to say?
options: Yes. Lumen Gentium calls the Church a sign of the unity of the whole human race.
Not really. The council meant unity for Church members only.
Sort of. It means all religions are the same, so the differences are gone.
chat.meaning: Lumen Gentium 1 calls the Church, in Christ, like a sacrament: a sign of union with God and of the unity of the whole human race.

Lumen Gentium.meaning: Vatican II's constitution on the Church; Latin for light of the nations

sacrament.meaning: a sign that, in Catholic teaching, also brings about what it shows

Mark.meaning: one of the four Gospels in the New Testament

sources.work: Second Vatican Council, Dogmatic Constitution on the Church

sources.quoted: Go ye into the whole world, and preach the gospel to every creature.

notes: Lumen Gentium 1 paraphrased (official English not public domain): confirm 'Christ is the Light of nations', 'the light of Christ brightly visible on the countenance of the Church', 'in Christ like a sacrament or as a sign and instrument both of a very closely knit union with God and of the unity of the whole human race', and the 'present-day conditions' sentence on social, technical and cultural ties.
'Not an eighth sacrament' (myth) and 'showing a reality and helping bring it about' are the script's gloss on 'veluti sacramentum'; confirm the Keeper is comfortable with it.
Mark 16:15 quoted from Douay-Rheims: confirm exact wording.

Unity thread: the day names 'the unity of the whole human race' from the council's own words, and marks it plainly as 'a Catholic hope, said in Catholic words' (unity in Christ), so it isn't dressed up as every tradition's view; the chat and fork reject both 'members only' and 'all religions are the same'.
